## Contract review brief — PR #37076 @ `84459523cd70acc86a20162638981d7e2a1a6473` (card #36713)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #36713: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #37076: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `84459523cd70acc86a20162638981d7e2a1a6473`
  · the check-runs on `84459523cd70acc86a20162638981d7e2a1a6473`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md, skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — if a `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` and the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

Rule change — if a `hits` path is under `.claude/**`: the PR body declares `Rule-change:` and you verify it against the diff.
  Write `Rule-change-verified: none` ONLY when no changed hunk alters what an agent may do without the maintainer
  (merge, bypass a check, change repository settings), what gets done and in what order (grading, dispatch, scope), or
  what must go to him (decisions, maintainer actions); process steps, scripts, wording, slimming and file moves are not rule
  changes. Write `ruled` ONLY when every such hunk copies the ruling the PR body quotes on its `Ruling-ref:` line — check the
  copy against the quoted words, do not re-rule it. Otherwise `yes`: the pull request then waits for the maintainer.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-objectstack/177ababb-cccd-573a-a846-cda17d8e5bbd/scratchpad/pr-37076/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `84459523cd70acc86a20162638981d7e2a1a6473`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md, skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md, skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json + none
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #37076, card #36713. Read: the card body and its three comments (triage 7102232941, claim 7140790532, os-dev-report 7141211804), the PR body, its four-file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base 896bfc4762, `main` at 159113f4fe; `main` has not moved under the three `hits` files, the cited spec and core files or the ratchet script since the merge base), and the 44 check-runs on the head.

Why the security line reads yes: the new paragraph teaches a declaration whose run-time effect is to hand child records to a new owner. In this platform the owner is the row anchor of sharing: the same bundle teaches that `owner_id` drives owner-scoped visibility and that `private` shows a record to its owner; the implementation is `packages/core/src/security/change-record-owner.ts`, and each cascaded write recomputes sharing as any owner change does. The refusal the paragraph names is keyed on a sharing model (`controlled_by_parent`), and the code's stated reason for it is access ("its access already follows its master, so it is not cascaded for access"). That is sharing behaviour taught under a path name that does not show it. What the paragraph does not do: it names no grant, widens no check, and says nothing on who may transfer (the caller's own transfer verdict still judges every cascaded row). The other hunks teach no security behaviour: the cut `(owned by parent)` comment removes a hint above a `controlled_by_parent` example and adds nothing.

Check-runs on the head: 28 success, 16 skipped, none failed, none pending. The skips are the expected ones: the path-filtered UI and docs lanes (Lint UI, Type Check UI, UI Published Artifacts, Build UI Deps, Build & E2E UI, Plan Test UI shards and the Test UI matrix, Build Docs), Dogfood Verify CLI and the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix, Temporal Conformance, the two opt-in jobs (Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness), the Schedule gate, and Queue verdict / Borrowed queue verdict, which run in the merge group.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: unchanged, right. The diff carries no schema, no validator and no generated baseline; `transferBehavior` and every refusal it teaches were published by PR #36525 (61722e9e8e).
- Public surface: the published `@objectstack/skills` text of two rule files and one eval fixture, right. Added: one paragraph and two table cells. Removed: restatement only (judged cut by cut under ④).
- Token ratchet: no ceiling row moved and `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` is not in the diff, right. Blob sizes read off the two trees: relationships.md 16805 to 16801 bytes (4202 to 4201 tokens, row 4203), field-types.md 14160 to 14156 bytes (3540 to 3539 tokens, row 3541). The lint lanes that host the ratchet, `check:skill-served-sections` and `check:skill-links` are success on this head.
- Eval fixture: one case appended, id 28, ids 1 to 28 unique and in order, the case carries the same keys as its neighbours.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` in both the PR body and the changeset: right. The diff publishes prose and a fixture from one released package and changes nothing a metadata author can write (the key itself shipped with #36525), so the kind is `none` and the level is `patch`. Check Changeset is success.

Clause-②: no

That declaration is right: no accept-set or consumer contract is narrowed or widened.

One wording slip in the changeset body, with no effect on the level: it counts "five comment or prose repeats" in relationships.md; the diff removes six (three comments shortened, three prose repeats).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, commit trailer: the landed commit carries the model-free `Claude-Session` and `Co-authored-by` pair. Accepted.
- Deviation, the eval case is 15 lines: the fixture keeps its two-space JSON form; net lines in `skills/**` are +3 against a budget of +10. Accepted.
- Deviation, `evals/README.md` not updated: it is a summary of what each fixture covers, outside the card's file surface, read by no gate. Accepted; a follow-up at the seat's discretion.
- Deviation, five families not measured locally (no built `dist/`): answered by the head's check-runs. `check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content` and `check:doc-formula-expressions` are hosted by Build Core and the lint lanes, all success.
- Deviation, report delivered before CI finished: all 44 check-runs are now complete, as listed above.
- One reading the PR body rests on a local run alone: `check:skill-eval-tokens`. Its CI step sits in Lint UI, which is skipped on this head, so no check-run measured that case 28's `must_contain` tokens are taught. Answered by reading instead: both tokens are literal in relationships.md at the head, `transferBehavior: 'cascade'` at line 179 and `controlled_by_parent` at line 183 (and many other lines).
- Out-of-scope finding (PR #36158 reads 4347 tokens against its own 4343 row once merged with `main`): not this diff's; it belongs to that PR's seat.
- SQL push-down: no code in the diff; nothing to judge.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Cited code, read on `main` and not reviewed: `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` (schema at 2330, refinements at 3399 to 3445), `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` (`refuseIneligibleTransferCascades`, 3952 to 3989, called from the object refinement at 5389), `packages/spec/src/data/user-action-transfer.ts` (`transferCascadeIneligibilityReason`), `packages/core/src/security/change-record-owner.ts` (`transferCascadeRelations`, `runCascade`), their tests (`field-transfer-behavior.test.ts`, `change-record-owner.test.ts`), and `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ChangeOwnerDialog.tsx` with its `en` strings.

**(a) relationships.md, the Change Owner paragraph, clause by clause**

- "`transferBehavior: 'cascade'` (default `'none'`)": holds. The schema is `z.enum(['none', 'cascade']).optional()` with default `none`; an omitted key parses to no key and reads as `none`.
- "on a child's `lookup` / `master_detail`": holds. The key is declared on the child's reference field, beside `deleteBehavior`.
- "has the parent's Change Owner dialog offer to move the child rows its previous owner owns too": holds. `transferCascadeRelations` lists the declared cascades to the parent; the dialog draws one tick per candidate ("Also move related records"); a ticked one makes `runCascade` move, to the new owner, the child rows that point at the moved record and carry its previous owner (`{ [field]: parent, owner_id: previousOwner }`), and no other row. "its previous owner" reads as the parent's, which is what the code does; eval 28 spells it out.
- "Parse refuses the key on other types": holds, an authored `'none'` included (field.zod.ts 3408; the test refuses it on `text`, `user`, `tree`, `number`). The `user` row of field-types.md rightly does not gain the key.
- "`cascade` on a `sys_*` reference": holds (3418; `'none'` is accepted there).
- "`multiple: true`": holds (3431; the patch-round refusal the card anticipated is merged, and the runtime never offers such a field either).
- "a child not offering Change Owner itself (a `controlled_by_parent` detail)": holds. `ObjectSchema` refuses `cascade` on every field of an object for which `transferCascadeIneligibilityReason` answers a clause: not structurally eligible, a `controlled_by_parent` detail, or `userActions.transfer` off.
- "declare it where children follow the parent's owner": sound guidance, and the sentence after it names the one place that reading would mislead (the `controlled_by_parent` detail).

Every refusal the skill names is one the merged code makes, and the card's older list is not copied. No refusal is omitted that would lead an author to write refused metadata: the structural arms the code also refuses (a child with no `owner_id` under `ownership` other than `user`, `managedBy`, `systemFields: false`, a `sys_*` child, a read-only `owner_id`, `userActions.transfer: false`) all fall under "not offering Change Owner itself", a child with no owner has no "rows its previous owner owns" to move, and the parse issue names the arm and its remedy. Tried to break it on the parent side: a reference to a non-`sys_*` parent that does not offer Change Owner parses and is simply never offered; the skill claims no refusal there, correctly.

field-types.md, the two rows: `transferBehavior` is listed on `lookup` and `master_detail` and nowhere else, which is exactly the type half of the schema.

**(b) the same-file cuts**

- Two `required: false` lines (the `lookup` and `tree` examples): no rule lost. The Relationship Types table states both optional, and the builder forces `required: true` only on a `master_detail` under `controlled_by_parent`; an omitted `required` on a `lookup` or `tree` is `false`. The one place `required: false` is load-bearing, the optional master at line 103, is untouched.
- Two code comments: `// Parent` / `// Child` keep the roles; "Invoice" and "Line Item" repeated the `name:` lines, and "(owned by parent)" is carried by `sharingModel: 'controlled_by_parent'` two lines below and the table's "Owned by".
- "whatever `inlineEdit` says": the rule survives in the same file at line 285, "`inlineEdit` only picks how a placed child's rows are entered", and objectstack-ui SKILL.md line 51 keeps the phrase itself. Eval 25's expected output still follows from the text and asserts neither phrase.
- "Set the string to override.": the code block directly above lists `'grid'` and `'form'` with what each does; nothing is lost.
- "purely": no content.
- The `inlineEdit: true` comment shortened to "auto (default)": the paragraph under the block states how the default picks.
- The two "Incorrect" code blocks, one sentence each: each sentence keeps the mistake and the remedy ("A line item on a `lookup` can exist without its parent: use `master_detail`."; "No `many_to_many` field type exists: use a junction object."), and both correct patterns stand in full above. The removed literal `type: 'many_to_many'` is only a `must_not_contain` token (eval 2), which needs no teaching; the bare `many_to_many` stays in the file.
- field-types.md, the autonumber example: the Autonumber section gives `CASE-{0000}` with its rendering (line 259) and the row keeps its pointer to it.
- field-types.md, "embedded" twice: the section heading "Embedded (JSON sub-objects)" and its lead sentence "Stored as JSON on the parent row, no separate table/FK" say it for both rows.

No cut removes a rule or a hint the file does not carry elsewhere. No finding.

**(c) eval case 28**

The expected output follows from the paragraph alone: the declaration on the child's reference field beside `deleteBehavior`, what the dialog then offers and which rows move, the `'none'` default, and the four refusals in the skill's own words. It agrees with the code: `opportunity` with no declared `sharingModel` offers Change Owner, so `account: { type: 'lookup', reference: 'account', transferBehavior: 'cascade' }` parses and is offered on `account`. "No hook" is the prompt's own framing and consistent with the file ("never an owner field copied by hooks").

Assertions: both `must_contain` tokens are taught by the bundle and are what a skill-led answer writes (the declaration in the bundle's single-quote form; the one refusal the paragraph names by example, which the prompt asks for with "where is that declaration refused"). `must_not_contain` holds for the expected output and for any answer that states the declaration.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract; fix on this prose face or leave):

- N1 (nit), relationships.md line 183: "(a `controlled_by_parent` detail)" reads as the definition of "not offering Change Owner itself", and no file in the bundle says what offering it means. The code refuses a `controlled_by_parent` detail even when it opens `userActions.transfer`, so the flat naming is right; the other arms are examples the parenthetical does not hint at. "such as", the wording the changeset and eval 28 already use, would say so.
- N2 (nit), relationships.md line 5 and the two field-types.md rows: the contents list names "Delete Behaviors" only and the rows carry no pointer, so the paragraph is found by reading that section; SKILL.md's router line (outside this diff) says "delete behaviors" alone.
- N3 (nit), eval 28 `must_not_contain: deleteBehavior: 'cascade'`: a correct answer that contrasts the two keys in code form would be rejected. The file's other cases use the same code-form convention for negative tokens, so the risk is small.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-36713-transferbehavior-skill`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYo86w1wqy2z2fMrryr`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · L1 · head `84459523cd70acc86a20162638981d7e2a1a6473` · 2026-11-24T19:17Z

Zone a4-A, card #36713. Read from the PR's diff and check-runs, not from the dev report.

1. **Shape.** 4 files: `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` (one Change Owner paragraph under Delete Behaviors: what `transferBehavior: 'cascade'` does in the parent's Change Owner dialog, the `'none'` default, when to declare it, the parse refusals), `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md` (`transferBehavior` on the `lookup` and `master_detail` rows), eval case 28, one `@objectstack/skills` patch changeset. Paid by same-file restatement cuts; no ceiling moved (relationships.md 4201 of 4203, field-types.md 3539 of 3541). Net +3 lines under `skills/**` against a budget of +10.
2. **Premise, measured.** PR #36525 merged (61722e9e8e); `transferBehavior` was taught nowhere in `skills/**` at `67154edeaf`. Every refusal the paragraph names was checked against the merged code (`field.zod.ts` refinements, `refuseIneligibleTransferCascades` in `object.zod.ts`, `transferCascadeIneligibilityReason`, `change-record-owner.ts`) by the contract review; the card's pre-patch list was not copied.
3. **Gates.** Check-runs on this head: 44, 28 success, 16 expected skips, none failed or pending. `check:skill-eval-tokens` sits in the skipped Lint UI lane; both case-28 `must_contain` tokens are literal in relationships.md (read by the contract review).
4. **Contract review.** PASS 7141869539 at this head (brief 7141848627). No must-fix, no should-fix; nits N1–N3 accepted. **`Security-touching: yes`**: the paragraph teaches a declaration that hands child records to a new owner, and the owner is the row anchor of sharing; the refusal it names is keyed on `sharingModel: 'controlled_by_parent'`. It names no grant and widens no check. The zone adopts the record and labels this PR `security` as the brief requires.
5. **Out of scope.** `skills/objectstack-data/evals/README.md`'s fixture summary does not name case 28; the changeset counts "five" repeats where the diff removes six — noted, not filed.
6. **Landing.** Tier H: `Security-touching: yes` takes it out of the low-risk skills arm. Handed to the seat session for an authorized approval; the zone does not ready, queue or arm it.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:AI 助手在建数据模型时,知道可以让「更换负责人」连带移交子记录,并知道哪些写法会被拒绝;此前它不知道有这个设置。
- 为什么做:属于「技能包教学」这条线,是「更换负责人连带移交」功能落地后欠下的教学补齐。
- 出错会怎样:AI 可能照着教学写出系统拒收的设置,保存时当场报错;可以直接撤回,只是文字改动。
- 要你做什么:批准合并。只改技能文字和一道评测题;按需人工批准处理,是因为契约审核判它「涉及权限」:教的是「更换负责人」连带移交子记录,负责人决定谁能看到记录。它没有放宽任何检查,也没有教授权写法。契约审核 PASS:记录 7141869539,Head-sha `84459523cd70acc86a20162638981d7e2a1a6473`。
